Thanks for reading our article! If you'd like to learn more about making a layer cake, check out our in-depth {{expert_interview_link:wikiHow Expert Interview Transcript Maria Short | interview}} with [v162228_b01].
#*You can make a layered cake with only one pan, but it will require patience and time, as you'll need to bake each layer separately, one at a time.<ref>[v162228_b01]. 22 November 2022.</ref>
{{whvid|Make a Layer Cake Step 0.360p.mp4|Make a Layer Cake Step 0-preview.jpg}}

#Line or grease your cake pans. Decide what size cake you'd like to make and get out the number of pans you'll need. You'll typically need 2 or 3 pans. Then cut parchment paper to fit the inside of the pans or spray the inside of each pan with baking spray. Greasing or lining the pan will ensure that the cakes don't crumble or tear when you remove them.<ref>https://www.completelydelicious.com/how-to-build-a-layered-cake/</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 1 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Make the cake batter. For a homemade cake, choose your favorite recipe and mix the cake batter. Ensure that the cake will make as many layers as you need or plan on doubling the recipe. To save time, combine 2 purchased cake mixes according to the packaged instructions.<ref>https://iambaker.net/how-to-build-a-layer-cake/</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 2 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Use a digital scale to divide the batter evenly among the pans. Once you've mixed your cake batter, set a prepared cake pan on a digital scale. Spoon some of the batter in and then set another pan on the scale. Keep filling each of your cake pans while you weigh them so the batter is divided evenly.<ref>https://www.completelydelicious.com/how-to-build-a-layered-cake/</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 3 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#[[Bake a Flat Cake|Wrap cake strips or towels]] around the outsides of the cake pans. Secure cake strips to the outside of each filled cake pan. If you don't have cake strips, tear an old kitchen towel into long strips and wet them. Wrap the damp strips around the outside of each filled cake pan.<ref>https://iambaker.net/how-to-bake-a-level-cake/</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 4 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Reduce the temperature to {{convert|325|F|C}} and increase the baking time. To bake flat cakes that are easily to layer and frost, turn the oven temperature down and bake the cakes for a little longer. Doing these things will prevent the cakes from cooking quickly in the center and puffing up.<ref>https://www.completelydelicious.com/how-to-build-a-layered-cake/</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 5 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Test the cakes and cool them completely. If you think the cakes have finished baking, insert a cake tester or toothpick into the center and pull it out. If it comes out clean and dry, the cakes are done. Then you can remove the cakes to cool completely.[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 6 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Chill the layers for up to 5 days. Once the cakes are completely cooked, remove them from the oven and turn them out onto a wire rack to cool. When the cakes are at room temperature, cover them with plastic wrap and put them in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour or up to 5 days.<ref>https://www.thekitchn.com/5-mistakes-to-avoid-when-making-layer-cakes-230655</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 7 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Trim away the excess dome from each cake. If your cakes baked faster in the center and domed up, you'll need to slice off the excess tops so each layer is even. Hold a serrated knife so the blade is horizontal and gently saw across the top of the cake so it's completely flat. Do this for each cake.<ref>https://food52.com/blog/3600-mastering-layer-cakes</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 8 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Cut the cakes into layers. If you'd like thin layers, use a serrated knife or cake leveler to cut each cake in half horizontally. This will also double the number of layers your cake will be.<ref>https://www.thekitchn.com/5-mistakes-to-avoid-when-making-layer-cakes-230655</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 9 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Mix your choice of [[Make Frosting|filling and frosting]]. Decide what flavor and type of frosting you'd like to use in between the cake layers and on top of the cake. For a variety of flavors, use one flavor for the filling and a different flavor for the top and sides.[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 10 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Place the first cake layer on a cardboard cake round or turntable. Cut a piece of cardboard to the same size as your cake pan and set it on a turntable. Spoon a dab of frosting on the center of the cardboard then set the bottom layer of chilled cake directly onto it. Put the cake top or cut-side down.<ref>https://www.completelydelicious.com/how-to-build-a-layered-cake/</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 11 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Spread frosting or filling over the bottom layer. Spoon 1/2 cup to 1 cup (125 to 250 g) of frosting onto the cake layer. Use an offset spatula to spread the frosting evenly across the top of the layer, but don't try to frost the sides.<ref>https://iambaker.net/how-to-build-a-layer-cake/</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 12 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Stack another layer of cake on top. If you're using a cake layer that you cut, lay it so the cut-side is facing down. It's fine if some of the frosting below the cake layer spills out over the sides.<ref>https://food52.com/blog/3600-mastering-layer-cakes</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 13 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Spread frosting or filling over the layer. Add another 1/2 cup to 1 cup (125 to 250 g) of frosting or filling to the newest cake layer and spread it so it's evenly covered. Continue to stack the cake layers and spread filling in between them until you've added all of your cake layers.<ref>https://www.completelydelicious.com/how-to-build-a-layered-cake/</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 14 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Spread a thin crumb coat over the top and sides of the cake. Put a large dollop of frosting onto the top of the assembled layer cake. Use an offset spatula to spread the frosting across the top and sides of the cake. The crumb coat should be so thin that you can see through to the cake.<ref>https://food52.com/blog/3600-mastering-layer-cakes</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 15 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Chill the cake for 30 minutes and frost the top and sides. Put the cake in the fridge to chill until the crumb coat firms up. Then remove it and spread the remaining frosting over the top and sides of the cake. This layer of frosting should be much thicker than the crumb coat.<ref>https://www.completelydelicious.com/how-to-build-a-layered-cake/</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 16 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Chill the cake for at least 30 minutes. Place the frosted layer cake in the refrigerator and let it chill until the frosting sets. This will make it easier to pipe frosting or add other decorations without the frosting sliding or melting.<ref>https://www.completelydelicious.com/how-to-build-a-layered-cake/</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 17 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Decorate the cake. Once your cake has been completely frosted, pipe frosting embellishments on the top and sides. If you like, sprinkle cocoa or candy sprinkles over the top. Consider garnishing the cake with flaked coconut, mini-chocolate chips, or chopped nuts.[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 18 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Transfer the cake from the turntable to a cake stand. Slide a cake lifter or large spatula under the cardboard base for your layer cake. Carefully lift it up in order to move the whole cake from the turntable. Set it down on your cake stand. Then slice and enjoy the layer cake.[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 19 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Store the layer cake at room temperature for up to 3 or 4 days. For the best texture, cover the layer cake with an overturned bowl or plastic wrap and keep it at room temperature. If you'd rather refrigerate it, store it in an airtight container for up to 1 week and let it sit out at room temperature before you serve it.<ref>https://www.savorysimple.net/perfect-layer-cake/</ref>[[Image:Make a Layer Cake Step 20 Version 4.jpg|center]]

added: The layer cake is one of the main creations in a baker’s repertoire. Circular, even layers of cake and frosting are layered and decorated, making it a popular birthday cake recipe. Creating a layer cake is harder than you might think, so use some baking tricks to make your layer cake stack up.
== Steps ==
=== Baking the Cake ===
#Purchase two to three round cake pans. Although you can stack cakes of any shape, traditional layer cakes are round. 8 or 9 inch round pans work best.
#Prepare your favorite cake recipe. Layer cakes often bring together complimentary cake and frosting flavors. You may want to combine lemon with vanilla or chocolate with raspberries.
#*Use butter, eggs and water at room temperature. Set the on the counter for about an hour before baking.<ref> http://www.kingarthurflour.com/tips/cake/</ref>
#Opt to use a box cake mix in place of a homemade recipe. If you are just learning how to assemble a layer cake, save some time by buying cake mix and pre-made frosting.
#Bake the cake according to the recipe directions. Take it out of the oven for 10 minutes. Then, loosen it from the pan and place the cake on a baking rack to cool all the way.
#*Test the cake by inserting a toothpick into the center. If it comes out clean, your cake is done.
#Lay your cakes upside down on the cooling rack so that they are flat, rather than domed.
#Wrap the layers of cake individually in plastic wrap. Place them in the refrigerator or freezer overnight. If you are short on time, do it for at least a few hours.
#*A cold cake is easier to frost.<ref>http://www.completelydelicious.com/2011/02/how-to-build-a-layered-cake.html</ref>
#Cut a round of cardboard the exact size of your cake pan. You can trace the cardboard and cut it out or buy a round cake platform at a kitchen or craft store.
#*If you don’t want to use a platform, slide pieces of parchment paper underneath the cake before you frost to cover your cake stand. Remove them before you serve the cake.
=== Making the Frosting ===
#Purchase or make your own frosting. Any thick, buttercream-like frosting should work. To make a quick version at home, mix together three cups (360g) powdered sugar and one cup softened butter.

#*Add one tsp. (5ml) vanilla extract and one to two tbsp. (15 to 30ml) of whipping cream once the mixture has been creamed. Beat in your mixer on medium speed for five minutes altogether.<ref> http://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/quick-vanilla-buttercream-frosting-recipe.html</ref>
#Place a dab of buttercream on the center of your round cardboard platform.<ref> http://www.marthastewart.com/275519/how-to-assemble-a-layer-cake/@center/276954/great-cake-recipes#189252</ref>
#Remove the cakes from the refrigerator. Unwrap the first one. Set it atop the platform.
=== Layering the Cake ===

#Decide how tall you want your layers to be. Make sure they are no higher than your shortest cooked cake. If the batter was not poured to exactly the same amount, one cake may be shorter than the others.
#*You can also cut each cake into two cakes if they are thick enough.

#Slice horizontally across the cake with a serrated knife. You may want to measure and mark the cake with a frosting dab if you aren’t confident you can cut in a straight line. Ensure saw through the domed top of the cake very gently.
#*If your cakes came out of the oven very level, you can skip the step of cutting them flat.
#Spread one cup of frosting onto the top of your first layer. Use an offset spatula and start with a big clump of frosting in the middle. Work the frosting out just past the sides of the layer.
#Make sure the layer is even. Then, set the second layer of cake on top of the frosting.

#Add one cup of frosting to the top of your cake. Stack layers of frosting and cake until you have reached the top of your cake. Remember the more layers you have, the more frosting you will need to make.
=== Frosting a Layer Cake ===
#Place the cardboard cake and platform on a Lazy Susan or rotating cake stand if you have one.
#Sit down and rotate the stand as you frost. It’s easier to judge the amount of frosting you are using if you frost near eye level.
#Add one cup of frosting to the top of your cake. Frost it to the edges.
#Frost the sides three to four inches at a time. Be generous with your frosting. Finish one section before turning the Lazy Susan and moving onto the next section.

#Opt to do a crumb layer if you are getting crumbs in your frosting. Wipe off excess frosting with your spatula. Cover with an even coat of frosting and then place your cake in the refrigerator for a few hours.
#*Remove it from the refrigerator and frost with a fresh coat layer of buttercream.<ref>http://iambaker.net/how-to-build-a-layer-cake/</ref>
#Lift the cardboard platform and place it on your cake stand.
#Decorate the cake as desired. Serve.
== Tips ==

*If you get cake crumbs make their way onto your spatula as you frost, you may not be using enough frosting. Scrape the offset spatula on a bowl to remove the crumb-filled frosting. Then, load the spatula again with a large amount of smooth frosting.
== Things You'll Need ==
*Round cake pans
*Cake Mix/recipe
*Buttercream/flavored frosting
*Cardboard platform
*Wire cooling rack
*Plastic wrap
*Cake stand
*Lazy Susan (optional)
*Offset spatula
*Serrated knife/cake leveler
*Refrigerator
*Cake decorations
